behavioral_evidence.claim: how it is computed
behavioral_evidence.value: From D_train, W_ij = number of consecutive (i,j) transitions over all training sequences, then W <- W + W^T. d_i = sum_j W_ij, M = sum_ij W_ij / 2. lambda_ij = ln((W_ij + alpha)/(d_i d_j/(2M) + alpha)). For a cell S_b, W_{i,S_b} = sum_{j in S_b} W_ij, D_b = sum_{j in S_b} d_j, lambda_{i,b} = ln((W_{i,S_b} + alpha)/(d_i D_b/(2M) + alpha)); the cell-pair version is rho_ab = ln((E_ab + alpha)/(D_a D_b/(2M) + alpha)) with E_ab = sum over i in S_a, j in S_b of W_ij. The baseline train-split L1 negative hit rate h1_train is estimated by holding out the last position of every training sequence, sampling one negative uniformly from items that anchor never interacted with, and counting the fraction of pairs with C1(negative) = C1(target) and lambda <= 0.

behavioral_evidence.claim: why it cannot leak

Validation and test interactions are used only after the SID file is frozen, to report the validation L1 negative hit rate and Stage-3 recall; they never enter W, tau, tau's quantile, the curvature, the candidate set or the accept decision. The Stage-2 encoder and codebooks are frozen before the repair, so no gradient from any split reaches the SID construction.

behavioral_evidence.claim: the proposed training-only signal
behavioral_evidence.value: Directed item-to-item transition counts from training-split user histories, converted to a popularity-adjusted pointwise-mutual-information log-ratio r(i,j), plus the training-user internal-holdout prefix-collision rate h0 used only to set the disjointness threshold tau.

behavioral_evidence.claim: how it is computed
behavioral_evidence.value: Training split only. For each training user history (i_1..i_T) add 1 to C[i_t][i_{t+1}] for every adjacent pair, after deleting each user's last transition (that deleted edge is the internal holdout and never enters C). T = number of retained transitions, p_i = rowsum(C)_i/T, q_j = colsum(C)_j/T, r(i,j) = log((C_ij + 1)/(T p_i q_j + 1)). The internal holdout gives, for each training user u with length at least 2, the pair (i_u, j_u) = (second-to-last, last) item; u is an internal negative hit iff P1(i_u) = P1(j_u) and C[i_u][j_u] = 0; h0 = hits / eligible users; tau = the h0-quantile of { r(i,j) : i != j, P1(i) = P1(j) }.

behavioral_evidence.claim: why it cannot leak
behavioral_evidence.value: All construction inputs come from the training split (transition graph, PMI profiles, SVD, Karcher means) and from the frozen baseline SIDs, which Stage 2 produced from the same split. The scalars tau and h0 are measured on training users' internal holdouts only, and each training user's last transition is deleted from C before anything is measured, so it cannot leak back into the graph. The validation split is read exactly once, after the patched SID table is frozen, to compute the diagnostic h1; that number is recorded and never fed into tau, into the candidate ordering, into the cap, or into any acceptance decision. Test interactions are seen only by the frozen Stage-3 evaluation.

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: use_behaviour_guard = 0, use_hyperbolic = 1: C_i is every cell, theta and A_ij are unused, the dS/dD accept test is bypassed, and the destination/partner are chosen by the hyperbolic centroid geometry alone. This is a pure curved re-partition and is exactly the falsified path; it isolates whether the behaviour accounting is doing the work. Not trained in this round.
ideas.ablation_both_on: use_behaviour_guard = 1, use_hyperbolic = 1, the mechanism exactly as specified, trained once for 3000 Stage-2 epochs on four cards followed by the frozen 150-epoch Stage 3 protocol, no early stopping.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: use_behaviour_guard = 1, use_hyperbolic = 0: d_H replaced by Euclidean distance, Karcher mean replaced by the arithmetic mean, and delta_hat recomputed as the Euclidean four-point deficit with the identical median-of-quadruples statistic, so the certificate stays self-calibrated and the control still fires. It isolates whether curvature changes the certified set, the centroids and the destination choice. Not trained in this round.
ideas.behavior_computation: One pass over the Stage-2 train sequences: n_ij = count of (item i immediately or within the session window followed by item j), n_i = sum_j n_ij, q_j = sum_i n_ij / Z; u_i[j] = clip(log((n_ij/n_i + 1e-8)/(q_j + 1e-8)), -10, 10), truncated to the 128 largest entries; A_ij = log((n_ij+n_ji+1e-8) Z / ((n_i+n_j) q_i q_j + 1e-8)) precomputed for stored pairs. S and D are recomputed from these lists on the current assignment. p_neg and theta are computed once from the same train transitions at epoch 300 and then frozen.
ideas.behavior_signal: Popularity-adjusted directed transition PMI between items (the behaviour graph), together with the split-neighbour count S and the disjoint same-cell count D derived from it.
ideas.cost_estimate: One-time precompute: sparse counts/PMI over 24556 items with at most 128 stored neighbours each (~3.1e6 entries) plus delta_hat over 1e5 quadruples (6e5 Poincare distances) = under 2 minutes of CPU, once. Per epoch: 256 Karcher means x 5 iterations x ~96 members (~8e7 flops) plus a guard pass of |V| <= 24556 items, each doing <=128 neighbour counts and ~96 cell-mate log-ratio lookups for dS/dD (~4.7e6 sparse lookups), vectorised to roughly 0.15-0.5 s per epoch on CPU/GPU, i.e. 8-25 minutes extra across 3000 epochs, +3-8% wall clock on four cards. Amortised per training step at 24 steps per epoch this is 6-20 ms, under 2% of a step. No new trainable parameters, no extra backward pass, no change to the 24556-item codebook update cost.
ideas.coupling_equation: c* = argmin_{c in C_i(theta)} d_H(b_i, m_c) with C_i(theta) = { code1(j) : A_ij >= theta, j in Nbr(i) }, theta = log((1-p_neg)/p_neg); accept swap(i,k) iff e^H(b_i; m_a, m_c*) <= delta_hat AND e^H(b_k; m_c*, m_a) <= delta_hat AND dS = S(swap) - S(now) < 0 AND dD = D(swap) - D(now) <= 0, where D counts same-cell pairs with A_ij < theta.
ideas.coupling_path: p_neg (behaviour, measured) -> theta -> candidate cell set C_i (behaviour log-ratio) -> destination chosen by curved nearest Frechet centroid d_H(b_i,m_c) (geometry) -> partner chosen by behaviour gain G (behaviour) -> Gromov thin-triangle certificate e^H <= delta_hat (geometry) -> monotone accept on dS, dD (behaviour) -> level-1 code exchange -> straight-through gradient into the encoder and the level-1 codebook -> SID tuple -> Stage 3. Removing behaviour empties C_i and the dS/dD test, leaving a pure curved reassignment; removing curvature makes the destination, the centroid and the certificate Euclidean. Both change which items move and where, hence the SID and the gradient.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: The idea is worth keeping only if the level-1 prefix is the bottleneck: then the certified swaps must lower the validation L1 negative-hit rate below the frozen train p_neg and raise the predictability of the true next SID's first token, which should show up as Stage3 test_recall@10 above 0.065. Observation: per-epoch S (split pair count) must be non-increasing by construction, the accepted-swap count must fall to near zero as training converges, and the validation L1 negative-hit rate must move in the same direction as recall.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: In the post-assignment repair step of the quantizer (once per epoch, level 1 only) and in the construction of the behaviour embeddings; never inside the residual argmin, so the Euclidean residual quantizer and levels 2..L are bit-identical to the baseline given the same seed except where a swap was accepted.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare ball of fixed negative curvature c=1: d_H(x,y) = arcosh(1 + 2||x-y||^2/((1-||x||^2)(1-||y||^2))), the origin exp/log maps, the Karcher/Frechet mean, and the Gromov four-point deficit delta_hat with the triangle excess e^H = 0.5(d_H(x,y)+d_H(x,z)-d_H(y,z)).
ideas.key_change: At the end of every Stage-2 epoch, after the usual Euclidean residual argmin, a guard recomputes one hyperbolic Frechet centroid per level-1 cell, picks for each split item a destination cell from its behaviour log-ratio candidates by hyperbolic nearest centroid, pairs it with the least-compatible member of that cell, and exchanges the two level-1 codes only if the Gromov certificate holds and the swap strictly reduces split behaviour-neighbour pairs without creating new disjoint same-cell pairs. Nothing else about the quantizer, the encoder, the decoder or levels 2..L changes.
ideas.leakage_boundary: Every statistic entering the guard (u_i, b_i, A_ij, tau, delta_hat, p_neg, theta, m_c, S, D) is computed from the Stage-2 training split only. The guard's own baseline is the pre-guard partition of the same run at epoch 300, which was produced without any validation or test signal. Validation and test interactions are never read during SID construction and never enter a centroid, a threshold or an accept decision; they are only used to report the L1 negative-hit rate and Stage3 recall as diagnostics.
ideas.motivation: The measured failure is not that the SID is coarse; it is that behaviour neighbours are split across level-1 cells, so the true next item sits under a prefix the generator cannot reach from the context prefix (high validation L1 negative-hit rate). Four earlier rounds tried to fix this by rebuilding prefixes with curved assignment, curved centroids or curvature-controlled levels, and all failed. This idea stops rebuilding. It keeps the baseline Euclidean quantizer, keeps the level-1 cell structure, and only permits a bounded set of size-preserving swaps that are certified by a curved test and are provably non-increasing in the split-neighbour count.
ideas.novelty: Hyperbolicity here is neither the assignment metric, nor a codebook-centroid update, nor a per-level curvature schedule, nor a cone. It is a CERTIFICATE FUNCTION: the four-point (Gromov) deficit measured on the training behaviour embeddings yields delta_hat, and a swap is eligible only when both items lie inside the delta_hat-thin triangle spanned by the two cell Frechet centroids. The behavioural failure count itself calibrates the pair bound (theta = logit of the measured L1 negative-hit rate), so no constant is tuned. The repair is a swap, so cell occupancy and codebook usage are conserved exactly, and the accept test is monotone (strictly decreasing) in the number of split behaviour-neighbour pairs.
ideas.observables: Per epoch: S (split level-1 behaviour-neighbour pairs), D (disjoint same-cell pairs), accepted swaps, cumulative fraction of items whose level-1 code differs from the epoch-300 pre-guard partition, mean reconstruction of swapped items versus non-swapped. Post-training: validation L1 negative-hit rate (the diagnostic that decides whether this is the same failure again), top-10 predictability of the true next SID's first token given the context prefix, and Stage3 test_recall@10 against 0.065.
risks: (a) The certificate or the dS<0 rule may certify almost nothing, making the mechanism inert and reproducing the baseline numbers; (b) swaps may damage per-item reconstruction so much that the encoder and the level-1 codebook degrade, hurting prefix quality; (c) p_neg measured at epoch 300 may be dominated by warm-up noise, making theta too lenient and dD almost vacuous; (d) the recall bottleneck may be at levels 2-3 rather than level 1, in which case a level-1-only repair cannot help; (e) one seed only, so a small positive or negative effect is inside seed noise.
ideas.safeguards: Poincare radii clamped to 1-1e-5; the arcosh argument clamped to >= 1+1e-9; the log map norm at the origin regularised to 1e-12; Karcher iteration step capped at (1-||m||)/2 with fallback to the member minimising the summed distance if the iterate leaves the ball; cells with one member use that member as centroid and empty cells are skipped; theta clipped via p_neg in [1e-6, 1-1e-6]; A_ij, G and u_i clipped to [-10,10]; delta_hat computed from a fixed seeded quadruple sample and frozen; a swap that would raise the epoch-mean reconstruction loss above the epoch median per-item reconstruction error is reverted (measured bound, no tuned constant); cells are never resized and splits are never merged, so codebook usage cannot collapse; the whole guard is a no-op when e < 300 and when |V| = 0.
ideas.spec_equations:
# ---- once, train split only ----
n_ij = directed transition counts from Stage-2 train sequences, keep top-128 per row
q_j  = sum_i n_ij / Z ;  n_i = sum_j n_ij
u_i[j] = clip( log( (n_ij/n_i + 1e-8) / (q_j + 1e-8) ), -10, 10 )
A_ij = log( (n_ij+n_ji+1e-8)*Z / ((n_i+n_j)*q_i*q_j + 1e-8) )
tau  = median_i ||u_i||_2
b_i  = tanh(||u_i||_2/tau) * u_i / max(||u_i||_2, 1e-12)        # b_i in B^64, c = 1
delta_hat = median over Q = 1e5 seeded quadruples (a,b,c,d) of
            0.5 * ( S2 - S1 ), S1 >= S2 >= S3 the sorted sums
            S1 = d_H(a,b)+d_H(c,d), S2 = d_H(a,c)+d_H(b,d), S3 = d_H(a,d)+d_H(b,c)
# ---- per Stage-2 epoch e ----
codes1 = Euclidean residual argmin, levels 1..L (unchanged baseline quantizer)
if e < 300: continue                                   # warm-up, guard off
if e == 300:
    p_neg = #{train transitions (i->j) : codes1[i] != codes1[j]} / #transitions
    theta = log( (1 - clip(p_neg,1e-6,1-1e-6)) / clip(p_neg,1e-6,1-1e-6) )
    S = #{train pairs (i,j) : codes1[i] != codes1[j]} ; D = #same-cell pairs with A_ij < theta
    freeze theta, S, D
m_c = KarcherMean({b_i : codes1[i]=c}) for the 256 level-1 cells, 5 iterations
for i in seeded order of V = {i : i has a neighbour j with codes1[j] != codes1[i]}:
    if i already swapped this epoch: continue
    a = codes1[i]
    C_i = { codes1[j] : j in Nbr(i), A_ij >= theta, codes1[j] != a }
    if behaviour_on and C_i is empty: continue
    cand  = C_i if behaviour_on else all_level1_cells
    c_star = argmin_{c in cand} d_H(b_i, m_c)
    if behaviour_on:
        k = argmax_{k in cell(c_star)} [ G(k,a) - G(k,c_star) ], G(k,c) = mean_{j in cell(c)} A_kj
    else:
        k = argmax_{k in cell(c_star)} d_H(b_k, m_c_star)
    if use_hyperbolic:
        e_i = 0.5*(d_H(b_i,m_a) + d_H(b_i,m_c_star) - d_H(m_a,m_c_star))
        e_k = 0.5*(d_H(b_k,m_c_star) + d_H(b_k,m_a) - d_H(m_c_star,m_a))
        delta = delta_hat
    else:
        e_i, e_k computed with ||.|| instead of d_H, delta = delta_hat_Euclidean
    if not (e_i <= delta and e_k <= delta): continue
    dS = S_after(i,k) - S ; dD = D_after(i,k) - D            # exact, two-cell neighbourhood only
    if behaviour_on and not (dS < 0 and dD <= 0): continue
    swap codes1[i] and codes1[k]; S += dS; D += dD; pin both at level 1 for epoch e+1
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: Stage-2 train interaction sequences; the current level-1..L code assignment, encoder latents and level-1 codebook vectors of the RQ-VAE; the precomputed behaviour embeddings b_i, pair log-ratios A_ij, tau, delta_hat and the frozen theta. Outputs: a repaired level-1 code assignment (a swap list, at most one swap per item per epoch), the pinned assignments for the next epoch, and the logged values of S, D, accepted swaps, changed-SID fraction and reconstruction of swapped items. No new tensor leaves the module.

specification.text: Fixed curvature c=1 Poincare ball. One-time from the Stage-2 train split: directed transition counts, popularity-adjusted PMI behaviour vectors u_i, hyperbolic behaviour embeddings b_i = tanh(||u_i||/tau) u_i/||u_i|| with tau = median ||u_i||, symmetric pair log-ratio A_ij, and delta_hat = median four-point deficit over 1e5 seeded quadruples. Guard off for the first 300 epochs (10% of the frozen 3000), at which point p_neg = train-split level-1 negative-hit rate of that pre-guard partition and theta = log((1-p_neg)/p_neg) are frozen for the rest of the run. From then on, once per epoch: recompute Karcher means m_c (5 iterations), for each split item i take C_i = {code1(j) : A_ij >= theta, j in Nbr(i)}, c* = argmin_{c in C_i} d_H(b_i,m_c), partner k = argmax_{k in cell(c*)} [G(k,a) - G(k,c*)], certify e_i and e_k against delta_hat, compute exact dS and dD over the union of the two cells' neighbour lists, and swap only if dS < 0 and dD <= 0. Swapped items are pinned at level 1 for the next epoch and then released. Everything is deterministic given a seed.

ideas.title: Gromov-certified, curvature-gated, occupancy-preserving level-1 repair swaps on an otherwise unchanged Euclidean RQ-VAE SID

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: The same Lorentz embedding, adjacency, curvature and exchange machinery, but lambda is replaced by 0, tau by -infinity and the potential by the geometry alone: an exchange is taken iff m_L(i;a,b) < 0 and m_L(j;b,a) < 0 (both items are already Lorentz-closer to the other cell) and cell sizes are preserved. This is a pure hyperbolic re-assignment of items that the Euclidean quantizer misplaced, with no behaviour gate and no disjointness predicate, so it isolates exactly the behaviour contribution.
ideas.ablation_both_on: The full run described in SPEC EQUATIONS: Lorentz embedding with K = 1/(4 delta_hat^2), Lorentz Voronoi adjacency, sigma = lambda - sqrt(K) max(0, m_L), tau from the baseline train-split L1 negative-hit rate, greedy lexicographic descent on Phi = (number of behaviour-disjoint geodesically adjacent cell pairs, number of behaviour-disjoint same-cell pairs), each item exchanged at most once. No arm is trained; these three switches exist in code and are exercised only by a unit test on a small synthetic batch, not by a training run.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: The identical graph, alpha, lambda, tau and potential, but the curved term is replaced by its Euclidean counterpart sigma_E(i -> b) = lambda_{i,b} + max(0, (||z_i - c_b||_2 - ||z_i - c_a||_2)/(||c_a - c_b||_2 + 1e-8)), and cell adjacency is Euclidean Voronoi adjacency (shared facet of the nearest-codeword diagram). Curvature is absent and the geometry term never grows with distance from the origin, so the accept set differs from the coupled one whenever curvature matters.
ideas.behavior_computation: From D_train, W_ij = number of consecutive (i,j) transitions over all training sequences, then W <- W + W^T. d_i = sum_j W_ij, M = sum_ij W_ij / 2. lambda_ij = ln((W_ij + alpha)/(d_i d_j/(2M) + alpha)). For a cell S_b, W_{i,S_b} = sum_{j in S_b} W_ij, D_b = sum_{j in S_b} d_j, lambda_{i,b} = ln((W_{i,S_b} + alpha)/(d_i D_b/(2M) + alpha)); the cell-pair version is rho_ab = ln((E_ab + alpha)/(D_a D_b/(2M) + alpha)) with E_ab = sum over i in S_a, j in S_b of W_ij. The baseline train-split L1 negative hit rate h1_train is estimated by holding out the last position of every training sequence, sampling one negative uniformly from items that anchor never interacted with, and counting the fraction of pairs with C1(negative) = C1(target) and lambda <= 0.
ideas.behavior_signal: Popularity-adjusted directed item transitions from the training split, symmetrised, with a cell-level aggregation; this is the co-consumption/transition signal, computed on training sequences only.
ideas.cost_estimate: Stage 2 and Stage 3 are untouched: 3000 epochs x 24 steps = 72000 optimizer steps, added per-step cost exactly 0. The repair is one post-hoc pass: transition-graph build O(nnz(D_train)), Lorentz Voronoi adjacency over C1=256 codewords at 3 geodesic probes and d=64, about 3.2e9 flops (well under one second on the four cards already allocated, about 20 s on CPU); item candidates at most N x mean degree about 1.5e5 distance evaluations; residual re-quantization O(#moves x d x (|C2|+|C3|)), bounded by 24556 x 64 x 512 in the impossible worst case and in practice a few thousand items. Total added wall clock on the order of one minute, under 0.5 percent of the run; amortized over the frozen 72000 steps this is roughly 1e4 flops per step, below 0.1 percent of a training step.
ideas.coupling_equation: admit(i in S_a -> S_b)  <=>  lambda_{i,b} - sqrt(K) * max(0, d_L(x_i, c_b) - d_L(x_i, c_a)) > tau  AND  Phi_after <_lex Phi_before, with lambda_{i,b} = ln((W_{i,S_b} + alpha)/(d_i D_b/(2M) + alpha)) and tau = Quantile_{1 - h1_train}({lambda_ij : C1(i) = C1(j), i != j}).
ideas.coupling_path: One inequality decides a membership change: sigma(i -> b) = lambda_{i,b} - sqrt(K) * max(0, m_L(i;a,b)), admitted iff sigma > tau and the potential decreases. The behaviour term lambda and the curved term sqrt(K) m_L are added inside the same margin that gates the same exchange, so removing behaviour makes the exchange a pure hyperbolic re-assignment, and removing curvature makes it a pure behaviour-driven re-assignment; neither can reproduce the coupled accept set. The same curved operator also supplies the adjacency graph whose disjointness count is the potential, so the two are coupled twice over one pathway.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: The idea is worth keeping only if, in the single coupled run, the validation L1 negative hit rate falls below the baseline value at unchanged level-1 cell sizes, the Stage-3 level-1 token accuracy rises, and test_recall@10 exceeds 0.065. Pre-registered kill conditions: if the baseline h1 (train estimate) is below 0.02 the cell contents are already coherent and no exchange can help; if the Lorentz nearest-codeword disagrees with the Euclidean assignment for fewer than 100 items the curvature term is inert and the result must be recorded as a geometry no-op, not as a negative on the mechanism.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: At the quantization/assignment step, in the final SID-assignment pass that runs once after Stage-2 epoch 3000 and before the SIDs are written for Stage 3. It decides membership changes at level 1 and therefore the prefix that Stage 3 sees; it also decides which item pairs are geometrically adjacent cells in the first place.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Fixed negative curvature K = 1/(4 delta_hat^2), where delta_hat is the Gromov delta of the training transition graph measured by the four-point condition on sampled quadruples of BFS-ball items; Lorentz model with inner product <x,y>_L = -x_0 y_0 + x.y and <x,x>_L = -1/K, exponential map at the origin, Lorentz distance d_L(x,y) = (1/sqrt(K)) arcosh(-K <x,y>_L), geodesic midpoint by Lorentz-normalised linear interpolation, and a signed geodesic bisector margin m(i;a,b) = d_L(x_i, c_b) - d_L(x_i, c_a) between the two codeword Voronoi cells. The curvature is derived from the measured tree-likeness (sqrt(K) delta_hat = 1/2), not tuned.
ideas.key_change: After the 3000th Stage-2 epoch and before SIDs are frozen for Stage 3, embed the frozen item latents and the frozen level-1 codewords into the Lorentz model with curvature derived from the measured Gromov delta of the training transition graph, and greedily execute item exchanges between Lorentz-geodesically adjacent level-1 cells whose behaviour log-ratio clears a bound tau taken from the quantile of the baseline same-cell log-ratios at 1 minus the baseline train-split L1 negative-hit rate. Each exchange is taken only if the behaviour-conditioned, curvature-scaled admissibility margin is positive and the pair potential (number of behaviour-disjoint geodesically adjacent cell pairs, number of behaviour-disjoint same-cell pairs) decreases lexicographically; residuals at levels 2 and 3 are re-quantized only for the moved items.
ideas.leakage_boundary: W, d, alpha, delta-hat, K, the baseline same-cell log-ratio distribution and the h1 used to define tau all come from D_train and from holdout tails inside D_train. Validation and test interactions are used only after the SID file is frozen, to report the validation L1 negative hit rate and Stage-3 recall; they never enter W, tau, tau's quantile, the curvature, the candidate set or the accept decision. The Stage-2 encoder and codebooks are frozen before the repair, so no gradient from any split reaches the SID construction.
ideas.motivation: The measured failure is not that the RQ-VAE codebook is badly placed; it is that the level-1 cell of an item contains behaviourally disjoint items, so a Stage-3 sampler that commits to a coarse token is forced into a candidate set whose members have nothing to do with the anchor. Earlier rounds attacked this by re-placing codewords (Frechet means), re-scaling curvature per prefix level, or re-ranking the assignment radially by context entropy, and none produced the required drop in the level-1 negative hit rate. This idea accepts the learned codebooks and the learned cell sizes as given and only repairs the membership of a small, explicitly admissible set of items, so the diagnostic cannot be improved by shrinking cells.
ideas.novelty: It is a post-quantization discrete repair, not a codebook update, not a curvature schedule, and not a radial re-weighting. Three properties are new here: (i) level-1 cell cardinalities are provably invariant (every accepted action is a two-item exchange), so the L1 negative-hit diagnostic is attributable to cell composition alone; (ii) the move set is generated only where the Lorentz nearest codeword disagrees with the frozen Euclidean RQ-VAE assignment, so the geometry does quantizer work rather than decorating it; (iii) admissibility is a single inequality in which the behaviour log-ratio must overcome a curvature-scaled bisector penalty, plus a lexicographic potential that is monotone non-increasing by construction. Unmoved items keep byte-identical baseline SIDs.
ideas.observables: Validation L1 negative hit rate (primary diagnostic, must be reported next to baseline); the unconditional L1 share rate (to show cell sizes did not move); the level-1 cell-size histogram (must be identical to baseline); number and fraction of items exchanged; number of behaviour-disjoint geodesically adjacent cell pairs before and after; number of behaviour-disjoint same-cell pairs before and after; the count of items where the Lorentz nearest codeword differs from the RQ-VAE codeword; Stage-3 level-1, level-2 and level-3 prefix token accuracy; test_recall@10.
risks: The frozen encoder latent may be near-Euclidean at the measured curvature, making the Lorentz-versus-Euclidean disagreement set empty and the repair a no-op; the tau quantile may be so high that no swap is admissible and the SID file is unchanged; swapping an item out of the cell the encoder chose breaks encoder-SID consistency and could cost reconstruction quality that Stage 3 partly relies on; the improvement may be confined to level 1 while L2/L3 negative hits dominate the recall loss; a single run with one seed cannot separate a small true gain from seed noise, so only a clear h1 drop plus a recall above 0.065 is interpretable.
ideas.safeguards: Clip the Lorentz inner product to at most -1/K - 1e-6 before arcosh and clip the arcosh argument to at least 1 + 1e-7; Lorentz-normalise midpoints with an epsilon on the norm and fall back to the Euclidean midpoint if the norm is degenerate; cap dL at 40 to avoid cosh overflow on far items; if M = 0 or fewer than 10 training transitions exist set alpha = 1 and skip the repair; if delta_hat is 0 use 0.5 hop as the floor so K stays finite; if h1_train = 0 set tau to the maximum observed same-cell lambda (strictest) and if h1_train = 1 set tau to the minimum (no-op); enforce that each item appears in at most one exchange so the permutation is an involution and no chains form; recompute Phi from scratch for the affected pairs and assert monotone non-increase, aborting the pass on any violation; never modify a codeword, never modify the encoder, and write a checksum proving that all unmoved rows and the level-1 cardinality vector equal baseline.
ideas.spec_equations:
# one-time, after Stage-2 epoch 3000
  W_ij <- count of consecutive (i,j) in D_train; W <- W + W^T
  d <- W 1 ; M <- sum(W)/2 ; alpha <- 2M/(N(N-1)) if M>0 else 1
  lambda_ij <- ln((W_ij + alpha) / (d_i d_j/(2M) + alpha))
  # curvature from the training graph only
  delta_hat <- 0.5 * max_{a,b,c,d in sample} (L1 - L2), L1>=L2 the two largest of
               {d_G(a,b)+d_G(c,d), d_G(a,c)+d_G(b,d), d_G(a,d)+d_G(b,c)}
  K <- 1/(4 * max(delta_hat,0.5)^2)
  # Lorentz embedding
  exp0(v) = ( cosh(sqrt(K)||v||)/sqrt(K), sinh(sqrt(K)||v||) v / (sqrt(K)||v||) ), exp0(0)=(1/sqrt(K),0)
  x_i <- exp0(z_i) ; c_a <- exp0(codeword_a)
  dL(x,y) <- (1/sqrt(K)) * arcosh( clip(-K <x,y>_L, min=1+1e-7) )
  # geodesic Voronoi adjacency (level 1)
  for each pair (a,b): u <- c_a + c_b ; g <- u / sqrt(-K <u,u>_L)   # midpoint on the geodesic
                       a ~ b iff the two nearest codewords to g are exactly a and b
  # cell behaviour + disjointness
  D_a <- sum_{i in S_a} d_i ; E_ab <- sum_{i in S_a, j in S_b} W_ij
  rho_ab <- ln((E_ab + alpha)/(D_a D_b/(2M) + alpha)) ; disjoint(a,b) iff rho_ab <= 0
  # baseline bound
  h1_train <- baseline L1 negative hit rate on the training holdout tails
  tau <- Quantile_{1 - h1_train}({ lambda_ij : C1(i)=C1(j), i<j })
  # potential
  Ndisc <- #{ (a,b) : a ~ b, disjoint(a,b) }
  Dsame <- #{ (i,j) : C1(i)=C1(j), lambda_ij <= 0 }
  Phi <- (Ndisc, Dsame) compared lexicographically
  # greedy exchange, one pass, deterministic
  used <- {} ; for (a,b) with a ~ b and disjoint(a,b), ordered by ascending E_ab:
     for i in S_a, j in S_b, ordered by descending m_L:
        m_i <- dL(x_i,c_b) - dL(x_i,c_a) ; m_j <- dL(x_j,c_a) - dL(x_j,c_b)
        if lambda_{i,b} - sqrt(K)*max(0,m_i) > tau and lambda_{j,a} - sqrt(K)*max(0,m_j) > tau
           and i,j not in used:
              tentatively set C1(i)=b, C1(j)=a
              re-quantize i: r <- z_i - c_b ; s_i2 <- argmin ||r - c_{2,k}|| ; r <- r - c_{2,s_i2} ; s_i3 <- argmin ||r - c_{3,k}||
              re-quantize j analogously into cell a
              recompute rho for every cell pair incident to a or b
              if Phi_after <_lex Phi_before: commit ; used <- used U {i,j}
              else: roll back
  # output: SID file with unmoved rows identical to baseline; Stage 3 unchanged

Outputs are a repaired level-1 token for each exchanged item, re-quantized level-2 and level-3 tokens for those same items, a byte-identical SID for every unmoved item, and a JSON diagnostic record containing h1_train, tau, K, delta_hat, the number of exchanges, Ndisc and Dsame before and after, and the unchanged level-1 cell-size histogram.

ideas.title: Curvature-gated, size-preserving exchange repair of the level-1 RQ-VAE token using training-only transition log-ratios and Lorentz geodesic bisectors.

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: Identical code path with the behaviour table replaced by text-embedding cosine similarity in every slot it occupies: w_hat_ij from cosine over the same neighbour sets, q_i from cosine-weighted agreement, LR replaced by cosine for the split/merge certificate, and B replaced by the measured train-split cosine quantile matching r0. This arm exists and must compile and run, but is not trained in this round.
ideas.ablation_both_on: The full mechanism above: behaviour-conditioned gyromidpoint position, Poincare distance with kappa=1, behaviour certificate with B=ln((1-r0)/r0) and the cell-radius guard. This is the single trained run.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: Identical code path with kappa->0: phi=identity, exp=identity, distance=Euclidean, gyromidpoint replaced by the Euclidean weighted mean, and the candidate score exp(-||v_i-c_k'||^2/(2*sigma^2)) with sigma the measured residual standard deviation. Behaviour signal and certificate unchanged. Not run.
ideas.behavior_computation: From TRAIN-split user sequences only: count consecutive directed pairs (i->j), symmetrise n_ij = n_ij^dir + n_ji^dir, marginals n_i, total pair mass 2N_pair, then LR(i,j)=ln(n_ij*2N_pair/((n_i+1)(n_j+1))) with add-one smoothing as a documented default; neighbourhood = smallest top-M_i covering 90% of sum_j n_ij, capped at the measured 95th percentile of M; weights w_ij=max(0,LR(i,j)) normalised per item. The coherence bound B is computed from r0, the baseline's TRAIN-split L1 negative-hit rate.
ideas.behavior_signal: Popularity-adjusted directed transition association between items, taken as a truncated, weighted behavioural neighbourhood graph per item.
ideas.cost_estimate: Zero added Stage-2 optimizer steps and zero added Stage-3 cost: 3000 epochs x 24 = 72,000 Stage-2 steps and the frozen 150-epoch Stage-3 protocol are unchanged, same token vocabulary and same sequence lengths. The repair pass is one shot after epoch 3000: graph build O(total train transitions), then 24,556 items x M_i neighbours (M_i typically 50-150) gyromidpoint iterations (10 Ungar steps) plus <= |C_i| <= 256 Poincaré distances: worst case about 5.7e8 scalar ops plus 3.7e6 integer certificate operations, under 2 minutes on one card if the per-item candidate block is vectorised, i.e. under 0.1% of Stage-2 wall clock and an amortised equivalent of about 1.7 ms per Stage-2 step at the frozen scale. Memory: one |I| x M_i index/weight block plus 24,556 x d ball coordinates.
ideas.coupling_equation: S_i(k') = q_i(k') * exp( -d_kappa( v_i , c_{k'} ) ), with q_i(k') = sum_{j in N(i)} w_hat_ij * 1[a_j^L = k'] and v_i = gyromid_{kappa}( {u_i} U {u_j}_{j in N(i)} ; {1} U {w_hat_ij} ), u_i = exp^kappa_{phi(mu_p(i))}( s*r_i ), c_{k'} = exp^kappa_{phi(mu_p(i))}( s*c^(L)_{k'} ), subject to the certificate Admit(i,k') = [dSplit_new <= dSplit_old] AND [dMerge_new <= dMerge_old] AND [at least one strict] AND [ ||r_i - c^(L)_{k'}||_2 <= R_{k'} ].
ideas.coupling_path: Behaviour weights enter the same scalar that curvature evaluates: the item's position v_i is the hyperbolic gyromidpoint of its own curved residual point with its behavioural neighbours' points (so the coordinate itself is behaviour-conditioned), and the candidate score multiplies the neighbour agreement count by the curvature-distorted distance from that displaced point to the candidate code. Removing behaviour sets v_i:=u_i and q:=uniform, so all candidates differ only by text geometry; removing curvature (kappa->0, phi=id, exp=id, distance=Euclidean, gyromidpoint=weighted mean) changes v_i and every d_kappa, so a different code wins. Either removal changes the accepted move set, hence the emitted SIDs.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: The recall loss is concentrated in last-token confusion among behaviourally coherent items whose text residuals sit where curvature distorts the comparison; if so, moving them must lower the validation L1 negative-hit rate while leaving every prefix token fixed, and Stage-3 test recall@10 must exceed 0.065 with a measurable fraction of moved items (expected single-digit percent). It is worth keeping only if (a) at least a few hundred moves are certified, (b) validation negRate@L1 falls, and (c) test recall@10 > 0.065; otherwise the no-op / small-move outcome is recorded with its numbers as a negative result.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: In the quantisation step, after Stage-2 converges and before Stage 3: it defines the geometry in which the deepest-level candidate codes are compared and in which the item's behaviour-displaced position is built. It acts on the discrete assignment produced by the RQ-VAE, not on the encoder or the codebook parameters.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincaré-ball exponential and logarithmic maps at a prefix anchor, Möbius addition, the Poincaré distance d_kappa(x,y)=(2/sqrt(kappa))*artanh(sqrt(kappa)*||(-x) xor_kappa y||), and the Ungar gyromidpoint, all with fixed negative curvature kappa=1 (unit curvature radius, so the effective curvature is -1/R^2 with R=1) and a scale s derived from the data maximum.
ideas.key_change: After Stage-2 epoch 3000, one deterministic pass re-assigns the last RQ level only, scoring each candidate code by q_behaviour(k') * exp(-d_kappa(v_i, c_k)), where v_i is the curved behaviour-displaced position of item i; a move is taken only if a train-split admissibility certificate (no increase in split coherent neighbours, no increase in same-cell disjoint neighbours) plus a cell-radius geometric guard both pass.
ideas.leakage_boundary: The graph, the weights, M_i, r0 and therefore B are all computed from TRAIN sequences; the Stage-2 encoder outputs and codebooks used are those fitted on TRAIN text embeddings; the repair never sees validation or test interactions, never sees validation item pairs, and never re-fits anything. Validation is read exactly twice, only to evaluate negRate@L1 before and after the repair, and that number is a reported diagnostic, never a gate, threshold or stopping signal. Test data is untouched until the frozen Stage-3 evaluation.
ideas.motivation: The measured Stage-3 failure is not a bad prefix tree but a bad local partition: behaviourally coherent items are split across cells while behaviourally disjoint items share a cell, and every previous attempt fixed it by rebuilding prefixes, which the last four rounds falsified. Stage 3 consumes only the item->SID tuple, so the map must move, but it can move in exactly one coordinate: the deepest code. This idea repairs only that coordinate, only where a training-split certificate proves the move cannot add a cross-cell coherent pair or a same-cell disjoint pair, and leaves levels 1..L-1 bit-identical.
ideas.novelty: Earlier rounds changed the codebook (Poincaré--Fréchet successor updates), the curvature schedule (CURVCTRL per-level curvature from prefix-transition scores), the radial coordinate of assignment (BRad-RQ context-entropy radius), or re-solved the assignment wholesale. This changes none of those: the codebooks, the encoder, the metric of the quantizer and the prefix partition are frozen; the only mutable object is the last-level token of a certified subset of items, and the decision score is a product of a training-transition agreement term with a Poincaré distance measured from a behaviour-displaced point (a hyperbolic gyromidpoint of the item with its behavioural neighbours), not a Voronoi re-assignment.
ideas.observables: Number and fraction of items whose deepest code changes; 100% identity of tokens 1..L-1 for every item (hard assertion); training-split split-coherent pair count and same-cell disjoint pair count, both non-increasing by construction; validation negRate@L1 before and after (the diagnostic that says whether this is the same failure again); per-item level-L conditional entropy of the next-token distribution under the frozen Stage-3 context, pre/post; final Stage-3 test recall@10 against 0.065. If zero moves are certified, the report says so and the run is a scored negative result, not a silent baseline.
risks: The candidate set C_i is built from neighbours' leaf codes, so items whose behavioural neighbours all live under different prefixes may yield no admissible move and the mechanism degenerates to an exact no-op (recall identical to baseline). The certificate may bind almost everywhere and admit only a handful of moves, giving no measurable effect. The cell-radius guard can veto precisely the boundary items the mechanism targets. Changing the last token for a few items perturbs Stage-3's last-level token statistics, which could cost more than it gains. The disjointness objective may be only weakly correlated with next-item recall. Fixed kappa=1 with data-driven scaling means the geometric term may be nearly Euclidean in effect, making the geometry-off comparison numerically close even though the code path differs.
ideas.safeguards: Clamp all ball coordinates to norm <= 1-1e-3 inside every exp map and every Möbius addition and renormalise after the gyromidpoint iterations; compute artanh in float64 with argument clipped to 1-1e-9; guard s against max_i||r_i||=0 by setting s=1 and skipping the repair (degenerate); skip candidates whose centroid is non-finite or whose cell has zero members (undefined radius R_k); require sum_{j in N(i)} w_ij > 0 or fall back to uniform w_hat over N(i); treat an empty C_i or a failed certificate as an explicit no-op with a logged reason; hard assertion that tokens 1..L-1 are bit-identical after the pass; monotone termination because each item is visited once and only its own pairs change, so total split and merge counts cannot increase; determinism by processing items in the fixed decreasing-mass order with ties broken by item id, so the result is seed-free and reproducible.
ideas.spec_equations:
```
INPUTS: train sequences; frozen E, C^(1..L), assignments a_i; frozen prefix centroids mu_p
1  n_ij, n_i, N_pair from TRAIN consecutive pairs (symmetrised)
   LR(i,j)=ln( n_ij*2*N_pair / ((n_i+1)*(n_j+1)) )
   M_i = min( argmin_M{ sum_{top M} n_ij >= 0.9*sum_j n_ij }, P95(M) )
   N(i)=top-M_i(n_ij);  w_ij=max(0,LR(i,j));  w_hat_ij = w_ij / sum_{j in N(i)} w_ij
2  r0 = negRate@L1(TRAIN, baseline SIDs);  B = ln((1-r0)/r0)
3  r_i = z_i - mu_{p(i)}
   s  = 7.6 / max_i ||r_i||            # artanh(1-1e-3)*2, keeps ||exp|| <= 1-1e-3
   u_i = exp^kappa_{phi(mu_{p(i)})}( s*r_i )
   c_k = exp^kappa_{phi(mu_{p(i)})}( s*C^(L)_k )      # prefix-local, k=1..K
   v_i = gyromid_{kappa}( {u_i} U {u_j}_{j in N(i)} ; {1} U {w_hat_ij} )   # 10 Ungar iterations
4  for i in order of decreasing sum_j n_ij  (each item visited once):
     C_i = unique{ a_j^L : j in N(i) } \ { a_i^L }
     for k' in C_i:
        q_i(k') = sum_{j in N(i)} w_hat_ij * 1[a_j^L = k']
        S_i(k') = q_i(k') * exp( -d_kappa(v_i, c_k') )
     k* = argmax_{k' in C_i} S_i(k'); continue if C_i empty
     dSplit(c) = #{ j in N(i) : LR(i,j) >= B  and a_j^L != c }
     dMerge(c) = #{ j in N(i) : LR(i,j) <  B  and a_j^L == c }
     R_{k*} = max_{ j : a_j^L = k* } || r_j - C^(L)_{k*} ||_2       # frozen baseline cell radius
     ok = (dSplit(k*) <= dSplit(a_i^L)) and (dMerge(k*) <= dMerge(a_i^L))
          and (dSplit(k*) < dSplit(a_i^L) or dMerge(k*) < dMerge(a_i^L))
          and (||r_i - C^(L)_{k*}||_2 <= R_{k*})
     if ok: a_i^L <- k*                       # levels 1..L-1 never touched
5  assert forall i: (a_i^1..a_i^{L-1}) unchanged
   report train split/merge counts, val negRate@L1 pre/post, moved count, then hand SIDs to Stage 3
negRate@L1(S) = |{(i,j) consecutive in S : a_i^1 = a_j^1 and LR(i,j) < B}| / |{(i,j) consecutive in S}|
```
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Input: TRAIN sequences, frozen Stage-2 encoder E, codebooks C^(1..L), frozen assignments a_i, prefix centroids mu_p, and the baseline train-split L1 negative-hit rate r0. Output: a repaired assignment matrix that is identical to the baseline except possibly in column L, the moved-item list, the certificate counts, and the validation negRate@L1 diagnostic; downstream it is the same SID token stream and vocabulary Stage 3 already consumes.

specification.text: (1) From TRAIN sequences only, count directed consecutive pairs, symmetrise n_ij, form the popularity-adjusted log-ratio LR(i,j)=ln(n_ij*2N_pair/((n_i+1)(n_j+1))). Neighbourhood N(i) = top-M_i by n_ij where M_i is the smallest prefix covering 90% of item i's transition mass, capped at the measured 95th percentile of that M distribution. Weights w_ij=max(0,LR(i,j)), normalised to w_hat. (2) Measure the baseline's TRAIN-split L1 negative-hit rate r0 with the same estimator used as diagnostic, and fix the coherence bound B=ln((1-r0)/r0). (3) Curvature: unit Poincaré ball, kappa=1 (fixed negative curvature, curvature radius 1). For item i, r_i = z_i - mu_{p(i)} (frozen Stage-2 encoder output minus its frozen prefix-centroid), scale s = 7.6 / max_i||r_i|| (derived from artanh(1-1e-3)). Anchor a=phi(mu_{p(i)}); u_i = exp^kappa_a(s*r_i); c_k = exp^kappa_a(s*c^(L)_k); v_i = gyromidpoint of {u_i} U {u_j : j in N(i)} with weights {1} U {w_hat_ij}. (4) Candidates C_i = distinct a_j^L over j in N(i), excluding a_i^L. (5) Accept at most one move per item, processed in decreasing transition-mass order, exactly once, with the certificate of the SPEC EQUATIONS block.

ideas.title: Prefix-preserving, certificate-gated hyperbolic repair of the deepest SID code, scored by a behaviour-displaced Poincaré point

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: use_behaviour=False: the boolean disjoint matrix is zeroed, sbar is set to tau everywhere and tau to 0, so dX == 0 and allowance == 0 for every candidate; the rule collapses to taking the curved nearest code that does not increase Poincare distance, i.e. the same curved operator with no behaviour information. The code path exists and is exercised by a unit test on a toy batch; no arm is trained.
ideas.ablation_both_on: the single formal run: use_behaviour=True, use_curvature=True, one candidate, 3000 Stage-2 epochs on four cards, frozen Stage 3 for 150 epochs, no early stopping, no seed repetition, no tuning of any constant.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: use_curvature=False: phi becomes identity, dP becomes Euclidean L2, lambda_l becomes the median Euclidean code distance; dX, sbar, tau and the whole veto are unchanged from the both-on run. The code path exists and is unit-tested; no arm is trained.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the TRAIN split only: for every user session in train, for every adjacent pair (x_t, x_{t+1}) add 1 to N_{x_t,x_{t+1}}; A = N + N^T; deg_i = sum_j A_ij; M = sum_{i<j} A_ij; s_ij = log((A_ij + 1)/(deg_i deg_j/(2M) + 1)). Store the top-64 neighbours by s per item; h0, tau, rho_l, lambda_l are computed once at epoch 0 from the same TRAIN matrix and the behaviour-free epoch-0 assignment.
ideas.behavior_signal: Popularity-adjusted directed item-transition log-ratio s_ij over consecutive in-session item pairs, symmetrised, used both as the disjointness predicate (s_ij <= 0) and as the coherence margin (sbar_i(b) - tau).
ideas.cost_estimate: Per step (batch 1024, D=3, K=256, d=32): the K-code distance evaluations already exist in the baseline argmin, now in the curved metric; add 1024*3*3 = 9216 Poincare distances (~30 flops each) and 1024*3*3*20 = 184320 sparse neighbour lookups for the veto against a precomputed boolean disjoint-edge matrix. About 3e5 flops per step, 2-4 ms batched on GPU, under 3 percent of a step whose transformer decoder forward dominates; overhead over 72000 steps (24 steps x 3000 epochs) is a few GPU minutes. One-off CPU: build the top-64 graph and the boolean veto matrix (24556 items, ~1.5e6 entries, 2-5 min), measure h0, tau, rho_l, lambda_l once at epoch 0 (~1 min). No new parameters; extra memory is the sparse veto matrix (~6 MB int32).
ideas.coupling_equation: admit(i: a->b, l) = [ dX_behaviour(i,b,a,l) <= 0 ] AND [ dP(u_i, v_b) - dP(u_i, v_a) <= lambda_l * max(0, sbar_i^behaviour(b) - tau) ], with dX_behaviour = sum_{j in Supp_i, s_ij<=0} ( 1[cell_l(j)=b] - 1[cell_l(j)=a] ).
ideas.coupling_path: item text residual -> exp map -> Poincare distance to candidate codes -> gap -> compared with lambda_l * max(0, sbar_i(b) - tau) -> compared again with dX (the behaviour-disjoint count) -> admit or stay -> straight-through into decoder and codebook update. The behaviour graph supplies s hence dX, sbar and tau; the geometry supplies gap and lambda_l; the admission is one boolean that is false if either the behaviour count or the curved margin is violated, so deleting the graph zeroes both the veto and the allowance (moves become pure curved nearest-code and the disjoint-pair leakage reappears) and deleting the curvature turns gap into a Euclidean gap (the budget no longer reflects prefix depth).
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If the failure really is same-prefix/disjoint-behaviour, the veto plus the curved budget rejects a few high-damage baseline moves and admits a few behaviour-coherent ones: SID churn stays between 3 and 15 percent (partition nearly the baseline), the validation L1 negative hit rate falls clearly below its epoch-0 value, and Stage-3 test_recall@10 exceeds 0.065 because the generator no longer spends prefix mass on disjoint items. If churn is ~0 the mechanism is inert on this pathway; if churn is large and the negative hit rate does not fall it is the same failure again and is recorded as such.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the RQ-VAE discrete assignment step at every level of every Stage-2 training step, i.e. inside the quantizer that produces the SIDs; never in a standalone loss and never in Stage 3.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare-ball distance dP at fixed negative curvature K = 1, composed with the exponential map at the origin exp^K_0 scaled by the measured rho_l; used as the assignment metric and as the travel budget in the admission inequality.
ideas.key_change: At each RQ level, instead of taking the nearest code outright, item i may move from its current code a to a candidate code b only if (1) the number of behaviour-disjoint items already in b (with the same shorter prefix) does not exceed the number in a, and (2) the Poincare distance increase from a to b is at most a behaviour-derived allowance scaled by a measured code-to-code Poincare scale. Otherwise the item stays where it is.
ideas.leakage_boundary: Everything that enters the SID construction (A, s, the boolean disjoint matrix, h0, tau, rho_l, lambda_l) comes from TRAIN interactions and from the epoch-0 encoder and codebooks, which were trained on TRAIN text features and TRAIN reconstruction targets only. No validation or test interaction, prefix or recall value is ever read into an assignment decision, and no derived constant is re-estimated after epoch 0. The validation L1 negative hit rate is computed only after training, as a post-hoc diagnostic, and is never fed back into the partition, into tau, or into a switch. There is no per-user adaptation at inference: the mask depends only on the TRAIN graph and the batch.
ideas.motivation: The measured failure is that the RQ-VAE places items in the same prefix even when their training behaviour is disjoint, so the Stage-3 generator spends prefix probability on items the user would never transition to. Earlier rounds attacked this by moving codebook positions (curved Frechet means), by changing the curvature value per level, or by re-scoring radius/assignment to build new prefixes; all rebuilt the partition and all failed. The remaining failure mode is the assignment step itself: it is unconstrained on the negative side. This idea keeps the baseline partition, the codebook positions and the Euclidean training losses, and constrains only individual re-assignment moves with (i) a hard behaviour veto that can never increase same-prefix behaviour-disjoint pairs and (ii) a hyperbolic travel budget that says how far an item may move to join a behaviour-coherent cell.
ideas.novelty: Not a codebook update (rejects poincare-frechet-successor-codebook), not a curvature schedule (rejects CURVCTRL-SID), not a radius/entropy assignment score (rejects BRad-RQ), not a new-prefix rebuild (rejects the whole last four rounds). It is a monotone admissibility operator on the discrete assignment: the curved metric appears only as the permitted travel budget inside an inequality, and the behaviour graph appears only as the negative-side count inside the same inequality, so neither can act without the other. The bound tau is self-calibrated from the baseline's own measured negative-hit rate, so no constant is tuned.
ideas.observables: (1) admitted-move count per level and the fraction of items whose SID tuple changes (churn), which must be small but nonzero; (2) validation L1 negative hit rate, the diagnostic that decides whether this is the same failure again, reported against its epoch-0 baseline value; (3) mean dP / mean L2 ratio, showing the curved term is operative rather than numerically Euclidean; (4) measured Gromov delta of the TRAIN transition metric as a context number, recorded and never used; (5) Stage-3 masked-prefix accuracy at L1 and full-SID predictability on validation; (6) Stage-3 test_recall@10 against 0.065.
risks: (1) The dX <= 0 veto can be satisfied trivially by staying put, making the operator inert and Stage 3 bit-identical to baseline - visible in the admitted-move counters. (2) h0 near 1 makes tau strict and leaves only zero-allowance moves, again near-inert. (3) For small residual norms the exp map is nearly linear, so geometry-off and both-on coincide; the mean dP / mean L2 ratio is reported, and a ratio within 1 percent means the result must be recorded as a geometry failure, not a behaviour failure. (4) The straight-through gradient stays Euclidean, so the encoder can drift and later reassign the same pairs; the veto is re-evaluated each step, so this shows up as oscillation, bounded but not eliminated by the no-move-unless-admitted rule. (5) A frozen 150-epoch Stage 3 may be insensitive to a small SID change, so a true effect may be unobservable in one run.
ideas.safeguards: clamp ||u||^2 and ||v||^2 to at most 1 - 1e-6 before arcosh; evaluate arcosh as log(1 + x + sqrt(x^2 + 2x)) with x = 2||u-v||^2/((1-||u||^2)(1-||v||^2)), add 1e-12 inside the log, and return 0 when the argument is at or below 1 + 1e-12. Guard rho_l with max(rho_l, 1e-6) and ||x|| with max(||x||, 1e-12). Items with empty support have created = removed = 0 and sbar = tau, so only distance-non-increasing moves pass, deterministically. Items without a level-l assignment at step 0 fall back to the baseline argmin. tau is clipped to max(tau, 0). If no positive same-cell pair exists, tau is set to the maximum observed s over all pairs, the run logs a degenerate-behaviour warning, and the mechanism is recorded as undefined rather than silently inert. If the veto matrix is empty the code takes the behaviour-off branch automatically and logs it, so a silent inert run is impossible. Assignment is applied level-ascending within a step so prefix_{<l} is always current, and the level-l counters are recomputed from the live A, never cached across steps.

No new parameters; the decoder interface is unchanged.

specification.text:
Let D be the RQ depth (e.g. 3), K the codebook size per level, d the residual dimension. Epoch 0 is the ordinary text-embedding RQ-VAE with no behaviour term and yields the initial assignment A0(i,l) = Euclidean argmin code at level l.
Step 1 (train-only behaviour graph). From TRAIN sequences count consecutive in-session directed transitions N_ij and symmetrise A_ij = N_ij + N_ji. Popularity-adjusted score s_ij = log( (A_ij + 1) / (deg_i deg_j / (2M) + 1) ), where deg is the symmetrised weighted degree and M the number of undirected edges (Laplace +1 is a documented default, not a tuned value). Behaviour-disjoint means s_ij <= 0. Keep for each item its top-64 neighbours by s as the sparse support of the veto (cap equal to the baseline context length, not tuned).
Step 2 (derived constants, all from TRAIN at epoch 0). h0 = fraction of same-L1-cell item pairs with s_ij <= 0 (the baseline negative hit rate, TRAIN only). Pos = { s_ij : s_ij > 0 and i,j share the L1 cell at epoch 0 }. tau = Quantile over Pos at probability q = h0, so a worse baseline demands stronger coherence; no tuning. rho_l = RMS norm of the epoch-0 level-l code vectors (measured, sets the exp-map scale so residuals do not saturate the ball). lambda_l = median pairwise Euclidean distance among epoch-0 level-l code vectors (measured, scales the allowance). Curvature K = 1, fixed, documented default; the Gromov delta of the TRAIN transition metric is recorded as a diagnostic only and never sets K.
Step 3 (curved images). phi_l(x) = exp^K_0(x / rho_l). For item i, u_i = phi_l(residual_l(i)); for code c, v_c = phi_l(c_l). dP(u,v) = arcosh(1 + 2K||u-v||^2 / ((1-K||u||^2)(1-K||v||^2))) / sqrt(K).
Step 4 (admission). For item i at level l with a = A(i,l), order all K codes by dP ascending and take the first m = D candidates (m equals the RQ depth, not tuned). For each candidate b != a compute created = number of j in Supp_i with s_ij <= 0, A(j,l) = b and prefix_{<l}(j) = prefix_{<l}(i); removed = same count for a; dX = created - removed; sbar_i(b) = mean of s_ij over the items j already in cell b sharing the shorter prefix (tau if cell b is empty); allowance = lambda_l * max(0, sbar_i(b) - tau); gap = dP(u_i, v_b) - dP(u_i, v_a). Admit iff dX <= 0 AND gap <= allowance; among admitted candidates take the smallest gap; apply with straight-through. Codebook positions, reconstruction loss and commitment loss stay exactly as in the baseline.
Step 5: nothing else changes. Decoder, Stage-2 schedule, Stage-3 protocol, seed: frozen.

ideas.title: Admissible geodesic re-assignment: a curved distance budget gated by a measured behaviour-disjoint-pair veto

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: Same code, BEHAVIOUR=false: w(i,b) := 1, tau := minus infinity so no pair counts as disjoint, Delta-D and Delta-R are still computed but the predicate is forced true (both switches stay implemented and unit-tested), and u_i is built from the frozen RQ-VAE encoder output e_i instead of z_i; the operator then performs a purely geometric content-space exchange. Not trained in this round.
ideas.ablation_both_on: The full operator as specified: behaviour points from PMI-compressed profiles, Poincare distance to hyperbolic Frechet cell means, behaviour weight w(i,b), and the exact Delta-D / Delta-R predicate with tau from h0. This is the single trained and evaluated run.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: Same code, CURVATURE=false: d_P becomes the Euclidean norm in ambient coordinates, Karcher means become arithmetic means, and u_i uses z_i without the tanh radial compression; behaviour weighting, tau and the admissibility counts are unchanged. Not trained in this round.
ideas.behavior_computation: Training split only. For each training user history (i_1..i_T) add 1 to C[i_t][i_{t+1}] for every adjacent pair, after deleting each user's last transition (that deleted edge is the internal holdout and never enters C). T = number of retained transitions, p_i = rowsum(C)_i/T, q_j = colsum(C)_j/T, r(i,j) = log((C_ij + 1)/(T p_i q_j + 1)). The internal holdout gives, for each training user u with length at least 2, the pair (i_u, j_u) = (second-to-last, last) item; u is an internal negative hit iff P1(i_u) = P1(j_u) and C[i_u][j_u] = 0; h0 = hits / eligible users; tau = the h0-quantile of { r(i,j) : i != j, P1(i) = P1(j) }.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed item-to-item transition counts from training-split user histories, converted to a popularity-adjusted pointwise-mutual-information log-ratio r(i,j), plus the training-user internal-holdout prefix-collision rate h0 used only to set the disjointness threshold tau.
ideas.cost_estimate: Zero added cost in all 72,000 Stage-2 steps (24 steps/epoch x 3000 epochs) and no change to the frozen 150-epoch Stage-3 protocol. One-time repair after epoch 3000: randomized truncated SVD of 24556 x 24556 with about 5e5 nonzeros (dominant term, 1-3 min on one card), 256 Karcher means x 15 iterations x ~96 members x 32 dims = 1.2e7 FLOPs, candidate gains about 5e7 FLOPs, gate counting about 1e7 integer ops, about 3 MB dense plus the sparse graph. Total under 5 minutes, roughly the wall clock of 5-10 Stage-2 epochs; no per-step recurrence.
ideas.coupling_equation: accept(i,k) = 1[G(i,k) > 0] * 1[DeltaD <= 0] * 1[DeltaR <= -DeltaD], with G(i,k) = w(i,b) * ( d_P(u_i, m_a)^2 - d_P(u_i, m_b)^2 ) + w(k,a) * ( d_P(u_k, m_b)^2 - d_P(u_k, m_a)^2 ), w(i,b) = max(0, rho(i,b) - tau), rho(i,b) = mean over j in cell b of r(i,j), and DeltaD, DeltaR the exact changes in disjoint same-cell pairs and in split behaviour-neighbour pairs caused by exchanging i in cell a with k in cell b.
ideas.coupling_path: Behaviour transitions -> C -> PMI log-ratio r -> two uses in a single decision: (i) the radial behaviour profile z_i -> u_i -> Poincare distance to Karcher cell mean m_b, multiplied by the behaviour weight w(i,b); (ii) the threshold tau -> the exact Delta-D and Delta-R counts that admit or veto that same swap. The product w(i,b) * d_P(u_i,m_b)^2 and the counts are the two halves of one accept/reject decision, so deleting the behaviour term turns the gain into a content-geometry gain and disables the gate, while deleting curvature turns the gain into a Euclidean gain on the same points and makes the means arithmetic. Either deletion changes which swaps are found or whether they are admitted.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If level-1 collisions between behaviourally disjoint items really cause Stage-3 misses, removing them under a one-for-one exchange with no cell-size change must lower the validation L1 negative-hit rate h1 below the baseline h0_val and lift test_recall@10 above 0.065; the gain should show up as a very small moved set (under 1 percent) with a large drop in disjoint co-location, not as a slightly better ER. If h1 does not fall, the mechanism is the same failure again and the round is recorded negative with its numbers.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Entirely inside the post-Stage-2 exchange operator: curved distance to hyperbolic Frechet cell means forms the swap gain, and Karcher means define cell position. Curvature never enters the RQ-VAE loss, the codebook update, the residual chain, or the Stage-3 model.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare ball of dimension d = 32 with fixed negative curvature kappa = 1 (unit ball, documented default); Poincare distance d_P(u,v) = arctanh(||(-u) + v||) with Mobius addition; exponential and logarithmic maps at the origin and at cell means; Karcher (Frechet) mean of a cell under d_P; the behaviour cloud enters the ball by the radial injection u_i = tanh(c||z_i||) z_i/||z_i||.
ideas.key_change: After the last Stage-2 epoch, build behaviour points u_i in the unit Poincare ball from PMI-compressed transition profiles, compute each frozen level-1 cell's hyperbolic Frechet mean, then greedily execute 1-for-1 cell exchanges whose behaviour-weighted Poincare gain is positive and whose exact Delta-D / Delta-R counts satisfy the admissibility predicate; only the tail tokens of moved items are re-derived, with the frozen level-2/3 codebooks.
ideas.leakage_boundary: All construction inputs come from the training split (transition graph, PMI profiles, SVD, Karcher means) and from the frozen baseline SIDs, which Stage 2 produced from the same split. The scalars tau and h0 are measured on training users' internal holdouts only, and each training user's last transition is deleted from C before anything is measured, so it cannot leak back into the graph. The validation split is read exactly once, after the patched SID table is frozen, to compute the diagnostic h1; that number is recorded and never fed into tau, into the candidate ordering, into the cap, or into any acceptance decision. Test interactions are seen only by the frozen Stage-3 evaluation.
ideas.motivation: The measured failure is not a bad codebook, it is a small set of level-1 prefix cells that hold items whose training behaviour is disjoint; every predicted-prefix collision with a behaviourally unrelated item is a miss the tail tokens cannot repair. Earlier rounds attacked this by re-quantising (new prefixes, Frechet codebook updates, per-level curvature control) and were falsified. This keeps the partition, codebooks, encoder and decoder intact and repairs only the empirical collision set, using curved behaviour geometry to choose which items trade cells.
ideas.novelty: The curved operation never touches the quantizer, the residual levels or the training loss; it acts only inside a post-Stage-2 exchange operator. That exchange is (a) cardinality preserving, so the prefix vocabulary, prefix frequencies and cell-size profile of the baseline are exactly unchanged, (b) capped at one move per item, and (c) admitted by exact integer counts on both sides of the partition (disjoint same-cell pairs and split behaviour-neighbour pairs) whose threshold is the baseline's measured negative-hit rate, not a swept constant. Prior candidates changed the assignment rule itself; this changes who sits in which cell, for a measured few items, and nothing else.
ideas.observables: Moved-item set and its size (under 2|S_neg|, expected well under 1 percent of 24556 items); Delta-D and Delta-R ledger per accepted swap; validation L1 negative-hit rate h1 against h0_val; behaviour-neighbour hop-distance and adjacency diagnostics of the patched table; Stage-3 learning curves; and finally test_recall@10 against the 0.065 bar.
risks: Near the ball's origin Poincare and Euclidean gains may rank swaps almost identically, making geometry-off indistinguishable and the coupling unproven; the Delta-R half of the predicate may reject every swap and turn the operator into a no-op; the internal-holdout h0 may misestimate validation collision structure, giving a tau that is vacuous or that shreds the behaviour graph; tail re-encoding of moved items can create fresh tail collisions outside the level-1 ledger; PMI is noisy for low-degree items; and moved items no longer sit where the encoder put them, so the decoder becomes inconsistent with the emitted SIDs (harmless at Stage 3, but must be documented).
ideas.safeguards: clamp every Poincare norm to 1 - 1e-7 and compute d_P through arctanh of a quantity clipped to [0, 1-1e-7]; if a Karcher step leaves the ball or fails to reduce Frechet variance, fall back to the best member and then to the origin; use alpha = 1 in the PMI denominator (documented default) so no log or division is undefined, and never evaluate r outside the candidate graph; if the h0-quantile is degenerate (h0 = 0 or 1), set tau to the minimum observed r plus a documented epsilon, record the degenerate flag, and let the gate decide; use exact int64 counting for Delta-D and Delta-R; never re-move an item and never change a cell size, with assertions on both; cap accepted swaps at |S_neg| and at N/2, both structural rather than tuned; freeze the Karcher means during the greedy loop so each gate check costs O(cell size); if zero swaps are admissible, emit the baseline SID table unchanged and record count = 0 as the result; if h1 is not below h0_val, record the round as negative with h0, h1, count, Delta-D, Delta-R and test_recall@10, without retuning tau or the predicate.
ideas.spec_equations:
pseudocode
  build C from training histories with each user's last edge removed; T=sum(C)
  p=rowsum(C)/T; q=colsum(C)/T; r[i,j]=log((C[i,j]+1)/(T*p[i]*q[j]+1))
  P1 = frozen level-1 SID; h0 = internal negative-hit rate; tau = quantile_{h0}(r over same-P1 pairs)
  X[i,:] = max(0, r[i,j]) for j with r[i,j] >= tau or r[j,i] >= tau
  Z = randomized_truncated_SVD(X, 32); c = 1/median_i ||Z[i,:]||
  u[i] = tanh(c*||Z[i,:]||) * Z[i,:]/||Z[i,:]||
  for each cell b: m[b] = KarcherMean({u[j]: j in b}, iters=15)
  for i, for b in {P1[j] : r[i,j] >= tau} \ {P1[i]}, for k in b:
      a = P1[i]; rho_ib = mean_{j in b, j != k} r[i,j]; rho_ka = mean_{j in a, j != i} r[k,j]
      G = max(0,rho_ib-tau)*(dP(u[i],m[a])^2-dP(u[i],m[b])^2)
        + max(0,rho_ka-tau)*(dP(u[k],m[b])^2-dP(u[k],m[a])^2)
  sort candidates by G desc; count = 0
  for (i,k,G) in order:
      if G <= 0 or moved[i] or moved[k] or count >= |S_neg|: continue
      dD = sum_{j in b\{k}} ([r[i,j]<tau]-[r[k,j]<tau]) + sum_{j in a\{i}} ([r[k,j]<tau]-[r[i,j]<tau])
      dR = sum_{j in b\{k}} ([r[i,j]>=tau]-[r[k,j]>=tau]) + sum_{j in a\{i}} ([r[k,j]>=tau]-[r[i,j]>=tau])
      if dD <= 0 and dR <= -dD: swap P1[i],P1[k]; moved[i]=moved[k]=True; count += 1
  for i in moved: re-encode c2,c3 with frozen level-2/3 codebooks on the new residual
  assert multiset(cell sizes) unchanged; assert set(P1) unchanged; assert count <= |S_neg|

specification.text: Inputs: frozen RQ-VAE codebooks (levels 1..3), frozen per-item SIDs, training-split directed transition counts C with internal-holdout edges deleted, training-user internal holdout pairs. objective:
Discover new mechanisms in which TRAINING-ONLY user behaviour and HYPERBOLIC geometry are computationally coupled to improve the RQ-VAE Semantic IDs used by a generative next-item recommender, with the real target of Stage3 test Recall@10 above 0.065.

One mechanism on the chain user behaviour data -> behaviour graph -> tree distance structure -> behaviour item embedding -> Gromov delta -> hyperbolic curvature -> text embedding into a hyperbolic RQ-VAE -> behaviour supervision -> SID -> Stage 3 -> recall@10. The candidate must address the measured failure directly: a move or assignment may only be taken when it does NOT increase the number of cross-cell neighbour pairs whose behaviour is disjoint. Concretely, whatever coupling is proposed, it has to carry an explicit admissibility predicate on the negative side, derivable from the training split (for example: a pair of items placed in the same cell must have a behaviour log-ratio above a bound that comes from the measured negative-hit rate of the baseline, not a tuned value), and it must report the resulting validation L1 negative hit rate as the diagnostic that decides whether the mechanism is the same failure again. Prefer a mechanism that leaves the baseline's partition untouched or nearly so; a mechanism that rebuilds the SID with new prefixes is exactly what the last four rounds falsified. The frozen Stage-2 budget is 3000 epochs on four cards and the frozen Stage 3 protocol is 150 epochs; one formal training run per candidate, no ablations, no tuning sweeps, no multi-seed runs. Stage 2 -> Stage 3 admission is technical validity only. test_recall@10 > 0.065 is the final judgement and a negative result must be recorded with its numbers.

papers.abstract: The success of models operating on tokenized data has heightened the need for effective tokenization methods, particularly in vision and auditory tasks where inputs are naturally continuous. A common solution is to employ Vector Quantization (VQ) within VQ Variational Autoencoders (VQVAEs), transforming inputs into discrete tokens by clustering embeddings in Euclidean space. However, Euclidean embeddings not only suffer from inefficient packing and limited separation - due to their polynomial volume growth - but are also prone to codebook collapse, where only a small subset of codebook vectors are effectively utilized. To address these limitations, we introduce HyperVQ, a novel approach that formulates VQ as a hyperbolic Multinomial Logistic Regression (MLR) problem, leveraging the exponential volume growth in hyperbolic space to mitigate collapse and improve cluster separability. Additionally, HyperVQ represents codebook vectors as geometric representatives of hyperbolic decision hyperplanes, encouraging disentangled and robust latent representations. The SLAM platforms we have utilized for this purpose are fast appearance-based mapping (FABMAP) and oriented fast and rotated short (ORB), both of which rely on extracting the features of the captured images in their loop closure detection (LCD) module. papers.abstract: Residual Vector Quantization turns continuous representations into discrete, multi-level token sequences. Yet most methods operate in Euclidean space, despite the coarse-to-fine structure of the resulting codes and the latent hierarchies present in many data domains. papers.abstract: Vector quantization is a technique in machine learning that discretizes continuous representations into a set of discrete vectors. papers.abstract: Residual Vector Quantization turns continuous representations into discrete, multi-level token sequences. Yet most methods operate in Euclidean space, despite the coarse-to-fine structure of the resulting codes and the latent hierarchies present in many data domains. papers.abstract: Most high-performance block-coding systems for image compression, such as JPEG, have been designed for software or dedicated digital hardware implementations where the data are already assumed to be available in digital format. papers.abstract: Vector quantization is a technique in machine learning that discretizes continuous representations into a set of discrete vectors. It is widely employed in tokenizing data representations for large language models, diffusion models, and other generative models. Despite its prevalence, the characteristics and behaviors of vector quantization in generative models remain largely underexplored. In this study, we investigate representation collapse in vector quantization - a critical degradation where codebook tokens or latent embeddings lose their discriminative power by converging to a limited subset of values. This collapse fundamentally compromises the model's ability to capture diverse data patterns. By leveraging both synthetic and real datasets, we identify the severity of each type of collapses and triggering conditions. Our analysis reveals that restricted initialization and limited encoder capacity result in tokens collapse and embeddings collapse. Building on these findings, we propose potential solutions aimed at mitigating each collapse. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive study examining representation collapsing problems in vector quantization.

papers.abstract: Machine learning algorithms have been shown to be highly effective in solving optimization problems in a wide range of applications. Such algorithms typically use gradient descent with backpropagation and the chain rule.
